name: Janecek v Freistaat Bayern (C-237/07)

jurisdiction.court: Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) – Second Chamber

description: Reference for a preliminary ruling from the German Bundesverwaltungsgericht (Federal Administrative Court): Mr Dieter Janecek, residing in Munich near a measuring station that recorded systematic exceedances of the daily PM10 limits, asked the Bavarian authorities to adopt an action plan under Directive 96/62/EC on air quality.
outcome: The CJEU recognised that citizens directly concerned have a right, enforceable in court, to obtain from the competent national authorities the drawing up of an action plan where there is a risk of the limit values or alert thresholds being exceeded. A fundamental judgment that opened the way to private “clean air litigation” in Europe (ClientEarth, DUH, Amis de la Terre, etc.).
